observations.text: SP, due to a not yet consolidated instrument cross-check on the ILS final approach, tracked the localizer and the glide path reactively instead of by anticipated corrections. CDI displacement reached 2.5 dots inside the FAF and the IP had to direct the intercept heading and the descent rate, which remains within the standard expected at this stage of training. Performance is marginal for the Training Section, since every correction followed an IP call and not the SP's own scan. Independent detection of the first CDI and GSI trend is expected to improve on the next sortie.

SP, applying the briefed ILS technique, established the aircraft on the localizer before the FAF and completed the final approach to DH with verbal prompts from the IP only. Localizer and glide path deviations peaked at 2 dots and computed final approach airspeed at 15 knots above the computed value, each corrected after the IP's call, with no control input by the IP at any point. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the ILS final approach IAW the Techniques and Procedures Manual without any direction or prompting by the IP. Errors were limited to 1.5 dots of localizer displacement, 1.5 dots on the glide path after the FAF and 12 knots above the computed final approach airspeed, all recognized and corrected in a timely manner by the SP. DH was respected and the missed approach was initiated by the SP. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew an accurate and timely ILS final approach IAW the Techniques and Procedures Manual and AFMAN 11-202 VOL3. Localizer and glide path were held within 1 dot from the FAF to DH, computed final approach airspeed within 8 knots of the computed value, and the level-off at DH was made 60 feet above the published altitude with no descent below it. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the ILS final approach with exceptional precision and a fully developed instrument cross-check. Localizer and glide path were held within 1/4 dot from the FAF to DH, computed final approach airspeed within 3 knots of the computed value, and DH was respected within 20 feet with an immediate and correct missed approach decision. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an incorrect lead point at the localizer intercept, did not establish the aircraft on final course before the FAF and chased the CDI with successive large heading corrections. Localizer displacement went beyond 2 dots to full-scale deflection and the glide path was left 2.5 dots high inside the FAF, with the result that the IP took the controls and re-established the approach. Further study of the ILS final approach technique and of the localizer intercept lead point is required.

SP, due to inadequate monitoring of airspeed during the approach, did not maintain the computed final approach airspeed after the FAF while attention remained on the glide path indication. Airspeed decayed 18 knots below the computed value and the descent was continued 150 feet below DH without the runway environment in sight, with the result that the IP directed the go-around and executed part of the missed approach. The ILS final approach could not be completed without the IP's assistance.

SP flew the ILS final approach within the desired standards for this sortie, completing the procedure to DH with the IP's verbal prompts only and without control input by the IP. Localizer and glide path deviations reached the 2 dot limit after the FAF and computed final approach airspeed reached 15 knots above the computed value, each recognized and corrected with delay after the IP's call. Marginal performance for the Training Section - earlier self-detection of the CDI and GSI trend is expected to improve on the next sorties.

SP flew the ILS final approach IAW the Techniques and Procedures Manual without prompts from the IP. Errors were limited to 1.5 dots of localizer displacement and 12 knots above the computed final approach airspeed after the FAF, recognized and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention, and DH was respected. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP intercepted and tracked the localizer accurately and completed the ILS final approach with proficiency and correct timing. Localizer and glide path were held within 1 dot from the FAF to DH, computed final approach airspeed within 8 knots of the computed value, and the missed approach was initiated at DH with no descent below it. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the ILS final approach with exceptional precision, well above the level desired for this stage of training. Localizer and glide path were held within 1/4 dot to DH, computed final approach airspeed within 3 knots of the computed value, and the level-off at DH was made within 20 feet of the published altitude with no descent below it. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an incorrect power and pitch setting at glide path intercept, did not establish the descent rate required to stay on the glide path after the FAF. The GSI reached full-scale low deflection and the aircraft descended 200 feet below the published DH, with the result that the IP took the controls and initiated the missed approach. The ILS final approach could not be completed without the IP's assistance.

SP, due to inadequate workload management during the approach phase, did not complete the approach checks and the ILS course and frequency set-up before reaching the FAF. The localizer was left untracked while the SP worked inside the cockpit, displacement went beyond 2 dots and the aircraft flew through final course, with the result that the IP directed the re-intercept and flew part of the approach. Further practice of the ILS final approach sequence and of task prioritization before the FAF is required.

SP, due to late and undersized drift corrections on final course, did not keep the localizer centered after the FAF. Displacement reached the 2 dot limit twice and computed final approach airspeed reached 15 knots above the computed value, with the result that the corrections were made only after the IP's verbal prompts and with delay. The approach was completed to DH without control input by the IP.

SP, due to a degraded basic instrument scan after prolonged en-route navigation, did not maintain the required attention split between the GSI and the primary flight instruments on final. The glide path was allowed to reach 2 dots high and the level-off at DH was made 200 feet above the published altitude, both recognized and corrected with delay after the IP's calls. The result was late acquisition of the runway environment, with the missed approach decision prompted by the IP.

SP flew the ILS final approach within the desired standards and without the IP's intervention. Localizer displacement of 1.5 dots and computed final approach airspeed 12 knots above the computed value after the FAF were each recognized and corrected in a timely manner by the SP, but the same glide path correction had to be repeated three times inside the FAF. Marginal performance for the Training Section - steadier power management on the glide path is expected to reduce the deviations on the next sortie.

SP flew an accurate and timely ILS final approach IAW the Techniques and Procedures Manual and AFMAN 11-202 VOL3, with a continuous instrument cross-check. Localizer and glide path were kept within 1 dot from the FAF to DH, computed final approach airspeed within 8 knots of the computed value, and DH was respected with a correct and timely missed approach. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the ILS final approach with exceptional precision and full anticipation of the drift and of the descent rate required. Localizer and glide path remained within 1/4 dot to DH, computed final approach airspeed within 3 knots of the computed value, and the DH decision was made within 20 feet of the published altitude with no descent below it. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to failure to set and identify the ILS frequency and final course before commencing the approach, tracked raw needle indications that did not correspond to the cleared final course. Localizer displacement went beyond 2 dots and the aircraft was 250 feet high at the FAF, with the result that the IP directed the correct set-up and executed part of the approach. Further study of the ILS final approach set-up IAW the Techniques and Procedures Manual is required.

SP, due to continuation bias in maintaining the approach after the flown parameters had deteriorated beyond the published limits, did not initiate the missed approach at DH. Computed final approach airspeed was 20 knots below the computed value and the glide path 2.5 dots high with the runway environment not in sight, with the result that the IP took the controls and flew the missed approach. The ILS final approach could not be completed without the IP's assistance.

SP, due to a pitch-only technique for glide path corrections without a matching power adjustment, did not hold the computed final approach airspeed after the FAF. Airspeed reached 10 knots below and 15 knots above the computed value in successive corrections and the GSI reached 2 dots, with the result that the deviations were corrected only after the IP's verbal prompts and with delay. No control input by the IP was required to complete the approach to DH.

SP, due to an incomplete mental model of the approach sequence that was not updated when the clearance changed, did not reconfigure the aircraft in time for the ILS final approach segment. Localizer displacement reached the 2 dot limit and the level-off at DH was made 200 feet above the published altitude, both recognized and corrected only after the IP's verbal prompts. The result was a late and compressed configuration inside the FAF, with the missed approach decision prompted by the IP.

SP, due to a slightly late lead on the localizer intercept, did not roll out exactly on final course and required two heading corrections after the FAF. Localizer displacement reached 1.5 dots and computed final approach airspeed 12 knots above the computed value, with the result of minor deviations recognized and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention. DH was respected and the missed approach was initiated by the SP.

SP, due to distraction by radio traffic while established on final, briefly interrupted the instrument cross-check and did not hold the glide path with the precision required for this stage. The GSI reached 1.5 dots high and the level-off at DH was made 150 feet above the published altitude, both recognized and corrected by the SP in a timely manner without the IP's intervention. Protection of the primary scan against secondary cockpit tasks after the FAF is required.

SP flew the ILS final approach accurately and with proficiency, within the desired standards and without the IP's intervention. Localizer and glide path were held within 1 dot and computed final approach airspeed within 9 knots of the computed value, but the airspeed approached the edge of the desired band twice inside the FAF. Marginal performance for the Training Section - more stable power management after the FAF is expected to improve on the next sortie.

SP flew the ILS final approach with exceptional precision and an uninterrupted instrument cross-check, IAW the Techniques and Procedures Manual and AFMAN 11-202 VOL3. Localizer and glide path were held within 1/4 dot from the FAF to DH, computed final approach airspeed within 3 knots of the computed value, and the DH decision was made within 20 feet of the published altitude with no descent below it. Above end of block MIF achieved.
